subject: Human Evolution
title: The Dawn of Farming
description: A fast breakdown of The Dawn of Farming for builders.

hook.text: About 11,000 years ago in the Fertile Crescent, someone planted seeds on purpose. Nothing was ever the same.

buildup.text: Wild wheat, barley, and legumes grew naturally in the region. People had gathered them for millennia.

discovery.text: Deliberate planting and selective harvesting gradually transformed wild plants into dependent crops.

twist.text: Farming spread not because it was better—early farmers were less healthy—but because it fed more people.

climax.text: Agriculture launched population growth, settlements, inequality, and eventually civilization as we know it.

punchline.text: A planted seed ended one era and began another.

quiz.question: Why did agriculture spread despite making people less healthy?
options: It fed more people per unit of land
